chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to rule in matters of inheritance regarding what was acquired by Islam from the wealth of a polytheist whom he left, which had not been divided before Islam: 'That he used to assign for the women and the men their shares from it, according to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.عَلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: According to the Book of Allah

ai.seo_question: How is the wealth of a convert to Islam inherited if it was not divided before their conversion?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) consistent application of the Quranic inheritance formula to *māl al-fay'* (booty or acquired wealth) that had not yet been distributed among the community, ensuring gender equity in shares. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Prophet’s Sunnah and the Imam’s practice align perfectly with the divine text, even in transitional periods of Islamic history. This ruling reinforces the principle that inheritance rights are fixed by divine decree rather than administrative discretion.
